draft.title: Documentary techniques
card: Interviews
An interview lets a person speak about their own experience. Filmmakers choose the questions and which parts of the answers stay in the final film.
Archival footage
Archival footage is older film or photos used to show the past. It can make a claim feel real, but the filmmaker still chooses which clips to use.
Voice-over
A voice-over is a narrator heard over the images. It can explain events and guide viewers towards a view of the subject.
Who speaks
Choosing who is heard shapes the representation. If only one group speaks, viewers may see the subject from that side alone.
draft.remember: A documentary is built from choices, so it shows its subject from a chosen point of view.

a.q: A documentary about a town's new dam includes interviews only with the company that built it. What is the likely effect?
opts: Viewers may see the dam from the builders' side
Viewers will see the dam from every side equally
Viewers will see the dam as unimportant
Viewers will trust the film less than archival footage
a.why: The choice of who speaks shapes the representation, so hearing only the builders leads viewers towards their view. It does not give a balanced picture, because other voices are missing.
a.clue: Think about whose voices are left out.

b.q: Over old black-and-white clips of a flooded street, a calm narrator explains that the town was never prepared. Which technique guides viewers most directly towards this view?
opts: The voice-over
The archival footage
The interview
The choice of who speaks
b.why: The narrator states the view in words over the images, which is a voice-over. The old clips show the past, but the clips alone do not say the town was unprepared.
b.clue: Which technique is a voice heard over the pictures?

a.best: Viewers may see the dam from the builders' side

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with the qualifier 'may'; every wrong option says 'will'. A student could pick it from the hedge alone, without knowing the idea.
The clue ('Which technique is a voice heard over the pictures?') restates the card's definition of voice-over. It gives the answer away instead of prompting thinking.
